title: RIKEN Integrates QunaSys QURI SDK Enterprise into Japan's JHPC-quantum Platform - Quantum Computing Report
gist: RIKEN adopted QunaSys's QURI SDK Enterprise as the primary hybrid quantum-classical software layer for Japan's NEDO/METI-funded JHPC-quantum project, unifying the Fugaku supercomputer and a 540-GPU ROQUO Blackwell cluster with heterogeneous QPU backends (IBM Quantum System Two, Quantinuum System Model H2) under vendor-agnostic middleware.

insights.claim: RIKEN's Center for Computational Science (R-CCS) has adopted QunaSys's QURI SDK Enterprise as the primary software layer for Japan's national JHPC-quantum project, funded by NEDO under Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A national research institute standardizing on a single commercial vendor's SDK is a strong endorsement that can drive further government and industrial adoption of QunaSys's software in Japan.

insights.claim: The integration connects the Fugaku supercomputer and the ROQUO GPU cluster (135 NVIDIA GB200 NVL4 nodes, totaling 540 Blackwell GPUs) with on-premises and cloud-hosted quantum processing units.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The scale of committed classical compute (540 Blackwell GPUs) alongside quantum hardware shows Japan is building serious hybrid HPC-quantum capacity, a data point for NVIDIA's exposure to quantum-adjacent infrastructure spend.
insights.locator: opening paragraph / Multi-Node Distributed Simulation bullet

insights.claim: The deployment follows the initial operational launch of the ROQUO GPU cluster in June 2026, indicating Japan's quantum-HPC buildout is proceeding on a defined sequential rollout schedule under NEDO's post-5G infrastructure program.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A visible sequencing (GPU cluster live mid-2026, software layer added by September 2026) gives a template timeline for how national quantum-HPC programs stage hardware-then-software rollouts.
insights.locator: Strategic Context within Japan's Society 5.0 Roadmap section

insights.claim: QURI SDK Enterprise enables cross-platform QPU portability, unifying workflow compilation across both superconducting hardware (IBM Quantum System Two at R-CCS) and trapped-ion hardware (Quantinuum System Model H2 at RIKEN's Wako campus) without requiring backend-specific code rewrites.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A hardware-agnostic orchestration layer that works across competing QPU vendors (IBM, Quantinuum) positions QunaSys as infrastructure middleware rather than a single-vendor tool, potentially giving it durable pull-through demand regardless of which QPU maker wins on hardware.
insights.quote: Cross-Platform QPU Portability: Enables unified workflow compilation targeting both superconducting architectures... and trapped-ion systems... without requiring backend-specific code rewrites.

insights.claim: QURI SDK Enterprise incorporates QunaSys's proprietary Quantum Selected Configuration Interaction (QSCI) and ADAPT-QSCI algorithm suites, targeted at active-space electronic structure calculations for materials science, quantum chemistry, and computer-aided engineering.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Proprietary algorithm IP embedded in the SDK (not just orchestration plumbing) gives QunaSys a defensible technical moat beyond commodity middleware.

insights.claim: Classical circuit simulation is offloaded via mpiQulacs across Fugaku's A64FX nodes using MPI, alongside NVIDIA cuQuantum-accelerated state-vector and tensor-network simulation across the ROQUO GB200 nodes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Heavy reliance on classical GPU simulation (cuQuantum) alongside real QPUs underscores that current quantum workflows still depend substantially on classical hardware, reinforcing NVIDIA's role as an enabling vendor in the quantum stack.

insights.claim: Access to the new software layer is currently limited to selected academic and industrial research groups under the JHPC-quantum Test User Program, indicating the platform remains in a restricted early-access phase rather than general commercial availability.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Restricted test-user access signals the program has not yet scaled to broad commercial usage, tempering near-term revenue expectations for QunaSys from this deployment.
insights.locator: Strategic Context within Japan's Society 5.0 Roadmap section
